questions.question: Which of the following is false regarding the neurotransmitter glutamate in the brain?

options.text: It is involved in excitatory neurotansmission
It is a minor neurotransmitter in the brain
It acts via both ionotropic and metabotropic receptors
Glycine binding to the NMDA receptor is essential for the receptor to respond to glutamate

suspectLines.text: Glutamate is a major excitatory neurotransmitter responsible for ~75% excitatory neurotransmission in the CNS.

questions.explanation:
Glutamate is a major excitatory neurotransmitter responsible for ~75% excitatory neurotransmission in the CNS.

Glutamate is the best-known example of excitatory amino acid neurotransmitters. It brings about its action via both ionotropic and metabotropic receptors.

Glutamate Receptors:

Ionotropic Glutamate Receptors
AMPA, Kainate receptors: Primarily permits influx of Na+ and efflux of K+ → EPSP (excitatory postsynaptic potential).
NMDA receptors: Permits ↑ influx of Ca2+ along with Na+ → EPSP (excitatory postsynaptic potential). Glycine binding to the NMDA receptor is essential for the receptor to respond to glutamate.

Metabotropic Glutamate Receptor (mGluR): Leads to either ↑ in IP3/DAG or ↓ cAMP.
